course.title: Yoga for Beginners
course.tagline: Build flexibility, strength and calm with daily yoga practice.

days.title: Your first yoga class
days.goal: Learn what yoga is and do your first gentle flow.
steps: Lay out a mat or a soft towel on the floor.
Watch the video and follow the slow moves.
Breathe in through your nose and out through your nose.
Rest in a lying down pose at the end for 1 minute.
days.task: Finish the video and rest lying down for 1 minute.
days.challenge: Do the video again tomorrow and breathe slower.

quiz.q: What is yoga?
options: Slow moves, breathing and stretching done together
quiz.explain: Yoga joins gentle movement with breathing.

quiz.q: How should you breathe in yoga?
quiz.explain: Slow nose breathing keeps you calm.

quiz.q: What should you do at the end of a class?
options: Rest lying down for a minute
quiz.explain: A short rest lets the body settle.

days.title: Breathe well: the base of yoga
days.goal: Learn slow belly breathing you will use in every class.
steps: Sit tall and put one hand on your belly.
Breathe in slowly and feel your belly rise.
Breathe out slowly and feel it fall.
Do this for 2 minutes, counting to 4 in and 4 out.
days.task: Practise belly breathing for 2 minutes.
days.challenge: Breathe in for 4 counts, out for 6 counts, 5 times.

quiz.q: What is belly breathing?
options: Breathing so your belly rises and falls
quiz.explain: Belly breathing is slow and deep.

quiz.q: Why breathe slowly in yoga?
options: It calms the body and mind
quiz.explain: Slow breathing tells the body to relax.

quiz.q: How long should you practise breathing today?
quiz.explain: Two minutes is enough to feel calmer.

days.title: Mountain pose: stand tall
days.goal: Learn mountain pose, the base of all standing poses.
steps: Stand with feet together and arms by your sides.
Press all four corners of your feet into the floor.
Lift your chest and let your shoulders drop down.
Breathe slowly and hold for 30 seconds.
days.task: Hold mountain pose for 1 minute.
days.challenge: Stand in mountain pose with your eyes closed for 20 seconds.

quiz.q: What is mountain pose?
options: Standing tall with feet together and arms relaxed
quiz.explain: Mountain pose is a tall, steady standing pose.

quiz.q: Where should your weight be?
quiz.explain: Weight across the whole foot keeps you steady.

quiz.q: What should your shoulders do?
quiz.explain: Relaxed shoulders help you stand tall.

days.title: Downward dog, the easy way
days.goal: Learn a gentle downward dog with bent knees.
steps: Start on hands and knees.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up high.
Keep your knees bent and your back long.
Hold for 20 seconds and breathe slowly.
days.task: Hold a gentle downward dog for 20 seconds, 3 times.
days.challenge: Pedal your feet: bend one knee, then the other, 5 times.

quiz.q: What shape does downward dog make?
quiz.explain: Downward dog makes a V shape with the body.

quiz.q: Why keep your knees bent?
options: It keeps your back long and safe
quiz.explain: Bent knees protect the back for beginners.

quiz.q: Where should you look in downward dog?
options: Toward your belly or your feet
quiz.explain: Looking down keeps your neck relaxed.

days.title: Child's pose: rest well
days.goal: Learn child's pose, the resting pose of yoga.
steps: Kneel on the mat and sit back toward your heels.
Fold forward and rest your forehead on the mat.
Stretch your arms forward or rest them by your sides.
Breathe slowly for 1 minute.
days.task: Rest in child's pose for 2 minutes.
days.challenge: Use child's pose whenever you need a rest in class.

quiz.q: What is child's pose for?
quiz.explain: Child's pose is a safe resting pose.

quiz.q: Where should your forehead go?
options: On the mat or on your hands
quiz.explain: Resting the forehead down helps you relax.

quiz.q: When should you use child's pose?
options: Only if the teacher says so
Whenever you feel tired in class
quiz.explain: You can rest in child's pose any time you need it.

days.title: Warrior 1: strong legs
days.goal: Learn warrior 1, a strong standing pose.
steps: Step one foot forward and bend the front knee.
Keep the back leg straight and the back heel down.
Lift your arms up high and look forward.
Hold for 20 seconds, then switch sides.
days.task: Hold warrior 1 for 20 seconds on each side.
days.challenge: Do warrior 1 with your back heel lifted if the floor version is hard.

quiz.q: What does warrior 1 build?
options: Strong legs and a tall chest
quiz.explain: Warrior 1 builds leg strength and opens the chest.

quiz.q: What should the front knee do?
options: Bend over the ankle, not past the toes
quiz.explain: The knee over the ankle keeps the pose safe.

quiz.q: Where should your arms go?
quiz.explain: Arms up high open the chest.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Your first flow
days.goal: Put week 1 together: link 5 poses into a short flow.
steps: Pick 5 poses you learned: mountain, downward dog, child's pose, warrior 1, and a stretch.
Move slowly from one pose to the next, breathing as you go.
Hold each pose for 20 seconds.
End lying down and rest for 1 minute.
days.task: Do your 5-pose flow and write down the order.
days.challenge: Do the flow without looking at your notes.

quiz.q: What is a yoga flow?
quiz.explain: A flow links poses with breath.

quiz.q: How long should you hold each pose?
quiz.explain: Twenty seconds is enough to feel the pose.

quiz.q: What should you do at the end of a flow?
quiz.explain: A rest at the end settles the body.

project.title: Your first flow
project.brief: Link 5 poses you learned into a short flow, hold each pose for 20 seconds, and end lying down for 1 minute of rest.

days.title: Sun salutation, step by step
days.goal: Learn the sun salutation, a classic series of moves.
steps: Start in mountain pose and breathe in.
Fold forward slowly as you breathe out.
Step back into a plank, then lower down.
Lift your chest, then press back to downward dog.
days.task: Do one slow sun salutation.
days.challenge: Do 3 sun salutations, breathing slowly.

quiz.q: What is a sun salutation?
options: A series of yoga moves done in order
quiz.explain: A sun salutation is a classic flow of poses.

quiz.q: How should you move in a sun salutation?
quiz.explain: Slow moves with breath keep it safe.

quiz.q: What comes after the forward fold?
quiz.explain: Stepping back moves you into the next pose.

days.title: Open your hips gently
days.goal: Learn two easy hip stretches.
steps: Try a butterfly: sit, feet together, knees out, hold your feet.
Try a low lunge: step forward, back knee down, hands on the front knee.
Hold each stretch for 30 seconds.
Breathe slowly and never force the stretch.
days.task: Do both hip stretches, 30 seconds each.
days.challenge: Hold the butterfly for 1 minute.

quiz.q: What is a butterfly stretch?
options: Sitting with feet together and knees out
quiz.explain: Butterfly opens the hips gently.

quiz.q: How long should you hold a stretch?
quiz.explain: Thirty seconds lets the muscle relax.

quiz.q: What should you never do in a stretch?
quiz.explain: Forcing a stretch can hurt you.

days.title: Twist gently for your back
days.goal: Learn a simple seated twist.
steps: Sit tall with legs out in front of you.
Bend one knee and put that foot outside the other leg.
Twist toward the bent knee and look over your shoulder.
Hold for 20 seconds, then switch sides.
days.task: Do a seated twist on each side for 20 seconds.
days.challenge: Do the twist after your next flow.

quiz.q: What does a twist do?
options: It stretches the back and belly gently
quiz.explain: A gentle twist stretches the spine.

quiz.q: How should a twist feel?
quiz.explain: A twist should feel like a gentle stretch.

quiz.q: What should your back do in a twist?
quiz.explain: A tall back keeps the twist safe.

days.title: Balance: tree pose
days.goal: Learn tree pose, a simple balance pose.
steps: Stand in mountain pose and shift weight to one foot.
Put the other foot on your ankle or your calf, not your knee.
Bring your hands together at your chest.
Hold for 20 seconds, then switch sides.
days.task: Hold tree pose for 20 seconds on each side.
days.challenge: Hold tree pose with your eyes closed for 10 seconds.

quiz.q: Where should your foot go in tree pose?
options: On your ankle or calf, never on your knee
quiz.explain: The foot goes below the knee to keep it safe.

quiz.q: What helps you balance?
quiz.explain: A still gaze helps you stay steady.

quiz.q: What should you do if you wobble?
options: Smile, put your foot down and try again
quiz.explain: Wobbling is normal; try again calmly.

days.title: Yoga for a calm morning
days.goal: Build a short morning routine to wake up gently.

video.title: 45 Min Full Body Yoga for Beginners

steps: Start with 5 slow breaths in bed.
Do a gentle stretch: arms up, side bends, forward fold.
Do 3 slow sun salutations.
Sit quietly for 1 minute and set one goal for the day.
days.task: Do the morning routine tomorrow when you wake up.
days.challenge: Do the routine for 3 mornings in a row.

quiz.q: Why do yoga in the morning?
options: It wakes the body up gently
quiz.explain: Gentle morning yoga wakes the body slowly.

quiz.q: What is a good morning stretch?
quiz.explain: Slow stretches wake the body safely.

quiz.q: How long should a morning routine be?
quiz.explain: Ten minutes is enough to start the day well.

days.title: Stretch your hamstrings
days.goal: Learn two easy stretches for the backs of your legs.
steps: Try a seated forward fold: legs out, reach toward your toes.
Try a standing forward fold with bent knees.
Hold each for 30 seconds and breathe slowly.
Keep your back long, not rounded hard.
days.task: Do both hamstring stretches for 30 seconds each.
days.challenge: Reach a little further each week, never forcing it.

quiz.q: What are hamstrings?
options: The muscles at the back of your thighs
quiz.explain: Hamstrings run down the back of the thigh.

quiz.q: Why keep knees bent in a forward fold?
quiz.explain: Bent knees keep the back safe.

quiz.q: How should a stretch feel?
quiz.explain: A gentle pull is the right feeling.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Your morning flow
days.goal: Put week 2 together: build your own 10-minute morning flow.
steps: Pick 6 poses you know and write them in order.
Add breathing: in as you lift, out as you fold.
Do the flow and time it.
End with 1 minute of quiet sitting.
days.task: Write your morning flow and do it tomorrow.
days.challenge: Do your flow for 3 mornings this week.

quiz.q: What should a morning flow have?
options: Gentle poses, breathing and a quiet end
quiz.explain: A morning flow is gentle and calm.

quiz.q: How many poses should it have?
quiz.explain: Six poses fit well in 10 minutes.

quiz.q: Why end with quiet sitting?
options: It settles the mind for the day
quiz.explain: A quiet minute helps you start the day calm.

project.title: Your morning flow
project.brief: Build your own 10-minute morning flow with 6 poses, breathing, and 1 minute of quiet sitting at the end.

days.title: Yoga for better sleep
days.goal: Learn a gentle evening routine that helps you sleep.
steps: Do a slow forward fold with bent knees.
Rest in child's pose for 2 minutes.
Lie on your back and hug your knees to your chest.
Breathe slowly for 2 minutes before bed.
days.task: Do the evening routine tonight before bed.
days.challenge: Do it every night this week.

quiz.q: Why do gentle yoga before bed?
options: It calms the body and helps sleep come
quiz.explain: Gentle evening yoga relaxes the body.

quiz.q: What is a good bedtime pose?
quiz.explain: Child's pose is calm and restful.

quiz.q: How should you breathe before bed?
quiz.explain: Slow out-breaths calm the body.

days.title: Open your chest and shoulders
days.goal: Learn two easy stretches for the chest and shoulders.
steps: Try a shoulder roll: roll shoulders back 10 times.
Try a chest opener: clasp hands behind your back and lift gently.
Hold the chest opener for 20 seconds.
Breathe slowly and keep your neck relaxed.
days.task: Do both stretches, 3 times each.
days.challenge: Do the chest opener after sitting for a long time.

quiz.q: Why stretch the chest?
options: Sitting a lot makes the chest tight
quiz.explain: Chest stretches undo tightness from sitting.

quiz.q: What should your neck do in a chest opener?
quiz.explain: A relaxed neck keeps the stretch safe.

quiz.q: How many shoulder rolls should you do?
quiz.explain: Ten slow rolls wake up the shoulders.

days.title: Warrior 2: strong and steady
days.goal: Learn warrior 2, a wide standing pose.
steps: Step your feet wide apart.
Bend the front knee over the ankle.
Stretch your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Look over your front hand and hold for 20 seconds.
days.task: Hold warrior 2 for 20 seconds on each side.
days.challenge: Move from warrior 1 to warrior 2 and back, slowly.

quiz.q: What is warrior 2?
options: A wide stance with arms out to the sides
quiz.explain: Warrior 2 is a strong, wide standing pose.

quiz.q: Where should you look in warrior 2?
quiz.explain: Looking over the front hand lines up the pose.

quiz.q: What should the back foot do?
options: Stay flat on the floor, toes pointing out
quiz.explain: A flat back foot keeps you steady.

days.title: Yoga for stress: slow and easy
days.goal: Use slow yoga to calm a busy mind.
steps: Sit and breathe slowly for 2 minutes.
Do a slow forward fold and hang your arms loose.
Rest in child's pose for 2 minutes.
Lie down and breathe slowly for 2 minutes.
days.task: Do this calm routine when you feel stressed.
days.challenge: Do it once a day this week.

quiz.q: How does yoga calm stress?
options: Slow breathing and gentle moves relax the body
quiz.explain: Slow yoga tells the body it is safe to relax.

quiz.q: What is a good pose when stressed?
quiz.explain: Child's pose is restful and safe.

quiz.q: How should you breathe to calm down?
quiz.explain: A long out-breath calms the body.

days.title: Chair yoga: yoga anywhere
days.goal: Learn yoga you can do sitting in a chair.

video.title: 15 Minute Full Body Yoga Stretch Class | Day 2 - 30 Day Yoga Challenge

steps: Sit tall in a chair with feet flat on the floor.
Do seated twists, shoulder rolls and neck stretches.
Stand behind the chair and do a gentle forward fold.
Breathe slowly through each move.
days.task: Do a 5-minute chair yoga routine.
days.challenge: Teach chair yoga to an older relative.

quiz.q: What is chair yoga?
options: Yoga done sitting or holding a chair
quiz.explain: Chair yoga makes yoga open to everyone.

quiz.q: Who is chair yoga good for?
options: Anyone, including older people and office workers
quiz.explain: Chair yoga suits all ages and bodies.

quiz.q: What should your feet do in chair yoga?
quiz.explain: Feet flat on the floor keep you steady.

days.title: Breathe deeper: 3-part breath
days.goal: Learn a deeper breath in 3 parts.
steps: Breathe into your belly first.
Then breathe into your ribs.
Then breathe into your upper chest.
Breathe out slowly in the reverse order.
days.task: Practise 3-part breathing for 3 minutes.
days.challenge: Use 3-part breathing at the start of your next class.

quiz.q: What is 3-part breathing?
options: Filling belly, ribs and chest in order
quiz.explain: Three-part breathing fills the lungs fully.

quiz.q: Why breathe into the belly first?
options: It is a rule with no reason
It helps the breath go deep
quiz.explain: Starting low helps the breath fill the whole lungs.

quiz.q: How should you breathe out?
quiz.explain: A slow out-breath keeps you calm.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Your 20-minute flow
days.goal: Put week 3 together: build your own 20-minute flow.
steps: Pick 8 poses you know and write them in order.
Add sun salutations at the start.
End with a twist, child's pose and 2 minutes lying down.
Do the flow and time it.
days.task: Write your flow and do it from start to finish.
days.challenge: Do your flow twice this week.

quiz.q: What should a 20-minute flow have?
options: Warm-up poses, standing poses and a rest
quiz.explain: A full flow warms up, works and rests.

quiz.q: How many poses should it have?
quiz.explain: Eight poses fit well in 20 minutes.

quiz.q: What should you do at the end?
options: Lie down and rest for 2 minutes
quiz.explain: A rest at the end settles the body.

project.title: Your 20-minute flow
project.brief: Build your own 20-minute flow with 8 poses, sun salutations at the start, and a twist, child's pose and 2 minutes of rest at the end.
checks: Ends with a twist and rest

days.title: Yoga for your back
days.goal: Learn gentle poses that help a stiff back.
steps: Try cat-cow: on hands and knees, arch and round your back slowly.
Try a gentle twist lying on your back.
Try child's pose for 2 minutes.
Move slowly and never force anything.
days.task: Do cat-cow 10 times, slowly.
days.challenge: Do the back routine every morning this week.

quiz.q: What is cat-cow?
options: Arching and rounding the back on hands and knees
quiz.explain: Cat-cow gently moves the spine.

quiz.q: How should cat-cow feel?
quiz.explain: Cat-cow should feel like a gentle stretch.

quiz.q: What should you do if your back hurts?
options: Move gently or stop and rest
quiz.explain: Gentle moves or rest keep a sore back safe.

days.title: Balance flow: tree and warrior
days.goal: Link balance poses into a short flow.
steps: Start in mountain pose and breathe.
Move to warrior 1, then warrior 2.
Move to tree pose on each side.
End in child's pose and rest.
days.task: Do the balance flow slowly, 2 times.
days.challenge: Hold each balance pose for 30 seconds.

quiz.q: What is a balance flow?
quiz.explain: A balance flow links steady poses together.

quiz.q: What helps you stay balanced?
options: Looking at one still spot and breathing slowly
quiz.explain: A still gaze and slow breath keep you steady.

quiz.q: What should you do if you fall out of a pose?
quiz.explain: Falling out is normal; try again calmly.

days.title: Yoga nidra: deep rest
days.goal: Learn a simple guided rest that relaxes the whole body.
steps: Lie down on your back with arms by your sides.
Close your eyes and breathe slowly.
Relax each part of your body from your toes to your head.
Rest quietly for 5 minutes.
days.task: Do a 5-minute guided rest today.
days.challenge: Do it before bed tonight.

quiz.q: What is yoga nidra?
options: A deep guided rest done lying down
quiz.explain: Yoga nidra is a rest that relaxes the whole body.

quiz.q: How should you lie in yoga nidra?
options: On your back, arms relaxed by your sides
quiz.explain: Lying down lets the body fully relax.

quiz.q: How long should you rest?
quiz.explain: Five minutes is enough to feel rested.

days.title: Yoga for strong legs
days.goal: Build leg strength with chair pose and warrior poses.
steps: Try chair pose: bend your knees and lift your arms, like sitting in a chair.
Hold chair pose for 20 seconds.
Do warrior 1 and warrior 2 on each side.
Rest in child's pose at the end.
days.task: Hold chair pose for 20 seconds, 3 times.
days.challenge: Do warrior 1 and 2 on each side, slowly.

quiz.q: What is chair pose?
options: Bending the knees and lifting the arms like sitting
quiz.explain: Chair pose builds strong legs.

quiz.q: What should your knees do in chair pose?
options: Point the same way as your toes
quiz.explain: Knees following the toes keeps the pose safe.

quiz.q: Why hold chair pose?
options: It builds strength in the legs
quiz.explain: Holding the pose makes the legs work.

days.title: Meditation: sit still for 5 minutes
days.goal: Learn to sit quietly and watch your breath.
steps: Sit tall with your eyes closed or softly open.
Breathe slowly and notice each breath.
When your mind wanders, bring it back to the breath.
Sit for 5 minutes and then open your eyes slowly.
days.task: Sit quietly for 5 minutes today.
days.challenge: Sit for 5 minutes every morning this week.

quiz.q: What is meditation?
options: Sitting quietly and noticing your breath
quiz.explain: Meditation is quiet time with your breath.

quiz.q: What should you do when your mind wanders?
options: Gently bring it back to the breath
quiz.explain: Wandering is normal; bring the mind back kindly.

quiz.q: How long should a beginner meditate?
quiz.explain: Five minutes is a good start.

days.title: Put it all together
days.goal: Build your own 30-minute yoga class.
steps: Pick a warm-up, 8 poses, a balance pose and a rest.
Write the order on one page.
Do the class and time each part.
Fix anything that felt rushed.
days.task: Write your 30-minute class and do it.
days.challenge: Teach your class to a friend.

quiz.q: What should a full class have?
quiz.explain: A full class warms up, works and rests.

quiz.q: Why write your class down?
options: So you can follow it and improve it
quiz.explain: A written class is easy to follow and fix.

quiz.q: What should you fix after testing?
options: Anything that felt rushed or unclear
quiz.explain: Small fixes make the class better.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final class.
steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 8 poses you can now do well.
Practise your capstone class once.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 8 poses you can do well now.
days.challenge: Do your capstone class from memory.

quiz.q: What is the capstone?
options: A final class that shows what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can lead a full class safely and calmly
quiz.explain: Leading a full class well shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone class once more, then rest.
steps: Lead your capstone class one more time.
Time each part and check your breathing.
Fix anything that felt rushed.
Rest well tonight.
days.task: Lead your capstone class and time each part.
days.challenge: Fix one thing that felt rushed.

quiz.q: Why practise once more?
options: Practice makes the real class calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
options: Your timing, your breathing and your poses
quiz.explain: Checking timing and breathing makes the class smooth.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you lead your best.

days.title: Capstone day: lead your yoga class
days.goal: Show what you learned: lead a full 30-minute yoga class.
steps: Welcome your students and set a calm mood.
Lead the warm-up, the poses and the balance work.
End with a rest and a kind closing.
Write a short report on how the class went.
days.task: Lead your capstone class and write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: What is the first step of your class?
options: A calm welcome and slow breathing
quiz.explain: A calm start settles everyone.

quiz.q: What matters most in the capstone?
options: Going as fast as you can
Safe poses, slow breathing and a calm voice
quiz.explain: Safe, calm teaching shows real skill.

quiz.q: What goes in your report?
options: What you taught and how it went
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Lead your own yoga class
capstone.brief: Lead a full 30-minute yoga class for a friend or family member: warm-up, poses, balance work, rest, and a short written report.
deliverables: A list of poses you can do well
A short video or notes from the class
